Theme

School & learning

form noun

of a word

also forms, form of a word, give the plural form, form the imperative, inflected form

classical

Quint. 1.4.29: quaedam tertiae dēmum persōnae figūrā dīcuntur ut licet, piget (Lewis & Short)
Varr. LL 9.52; 9.55 (Lewis & Short: “form of a word, inflection”)
Traupman 246

figūra, figūrae f.

noun, first declension

a form of a word, an inflected form

The shape a word takes in inflection: give the plural form of gaudium, dā (dīc) figūram plūrālem «gaudium» nōminis (Traupman 246). A form is simple or compound: figūra est aut simplex, ut «doctus», aut composita, ut «indoctus» (Traupman 246). To form the imperative is facere imperātīvum (Traupman 246).

Examples

  • quaedam tertiae dēmum persōnae figūrā dīcuntur ut licet, piget

    some are said only in the form of the third person, as licet, pigetQuint. 1.4.29 (Lewis & Short)

  • Quibus figūrīs «ōdī» eget?

    What forms does “ōdī” lack?Traupman 230

See also ending, compound, declension, conjugation.
